title: Grateful Dead Live at Red Rocks Amphitheatre on 1982-07-29
lineage: FOB - Senn 421's> Sony TC-D5 (at mouth of the stage)> Nak Dragon Playback> HHB CDR-850 (no DAT gen)> CDR

ai_review.summary: Excellent audience recording captures a rain‑soaked July ’82 Red Rocks show with smoking Crazy Fingers, Cold Rain > Samson and an epic Other One.
ai_review.review: The audience tape, recorded by Jim Wise, is surprisingly clear and well‑balanced despite the inevitable crowd chatter, delivering deep bass and crisp guitar tones. Musically the night is a high‑energy highlight of the Red Rocks run – a slow‑grooving first set that builds into a second‑set powerhouse featuring Cold Rain > Samson, Crazy Fingers, The Other One and Stranger. Reviewers rave about Jerry’s soaring leads, Phil’s booming bass ramp‑up, and the overall rain‑charged atmosphere.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 4–5) and enthusiastic comments about both performance and sound quality; strong weighting toward a superb show with good‑to‑excellent recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑balanced tape with deep bass and crisp guitar; occasional crowd chatter and chatty mic moments noted, but overall listenable and praised as ‘excellent sounding audience recording’.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts slow and spacey under rain, building momentum; second set erupts with high‑energy transitions (Cold Rain > Samson into Crazy Fingers) and a powerful Other One, delivering an arc that many reviewers call the highlight of the summer ’82 run.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for soaring leads on Crazy Fingers, solid licks on Samson/Delilah, and overall great form; his guitar cuts through the fog and rain‑filled ambience.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a perfect bass ramp‑up into The Other One and deep, powerful low end that many reviewers describe as ‘deep bass’ and ‘Phil bombs’.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm guitar sometimes sits low in the mix on this audience tape, but his timing and vocal contributions are appreciated; occasional comments about Bobby being overwhelmed by the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s vocals are mentioned as a bit low for some listeners, yet his keyboard work underpins the jam sections and adds to the ‘trippy’ atmosphere.
band_member_comments.Drums: Kreutzmann’s drumming is highlighted for taking charge during Samson/Delilah transitions and delivering high‑energy, tight drum breaks; the short Space segment is praised as sweet and effective.
